title: Overlap-Refresh: Decoupling Window Shifts from Full KV Refresh in Diffusion Language Models

contributions.purpose: Diagnose the inefficiency in Window-Diffusion's phase-boundary handling.
contributions.mechanism: Identify that Window-Diffusion couples window shifts with full KV refresh via a single refresh_cycle parameter, and analyze naive refresh reduction.
contributions.evaluation: Show that naive refresh reduction degrades both generation quality and speed.
contributions.source_quote: We identify the coupling inefficiency in Window-Diffusion's phase boundary operations and show that naive refresh reduction degrades both quality and speed.

contributions.purpose: Enable efficient scheduling without sacrificing generation quality.
contributions.mechanism: Propose Overlap-Refresh, decoupling window shift frequency from KV refresh frequency via two independent scheduling parameters (shift_interval and refresh_interval).
contributions.evaluation: Presented as a decoupled scheduler; validated via downstream throughput/quality results.
contributions.source_quote: We propose Overlap-Refresh, which decouples window shift frequency from KV refresh frequency via two independent scheduling parameters.

contributions.purpose: Cheaply update the KV cache at shift-only boundaries.
contributions.mechanism: Introduce delta-prefill, computing KV only for newly entered tokens while reusing cached KV for overlap tokens, giving O(|N| x C) cost versus O(C^2) for full refresh.
contributions.evaluation: Runtime analysis confirms delta-prefill is 3.3x cheaper than full refresh.
contributions.source_quote: We introduce delta-prefill, an efficient operation that computes KV only for newly entered tokens, achieving 3.3x cost reduction compared to full refresh.

contributions.purpose: Demonstrate end-to-end throughput gains at near-baseline quality.
contributions.mechanism: Evaluate Overlap-Refresh on MBPP code generation against the Window-Diffusion baseline.
contributions.evaluation: 6.0% throughput improvement (8.59 vs 8.10 tokens/sec) while preserving quality within 0.6 percentage points (54.4% vs 55.0% Pass@1).
contributions.source_quote: We demonstrate 6.0% throughput improvement on MBPP while preserving generation quality within 0.6 percentage points of the Window-Diffusion baseline.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Our work builds upon Window-Diffusion by decoupling window shifts from KV refresh operations, enabling more efficient scheduling without sacrificing quality.
Our delta-prefill mechanism draws inspiration from incremental KV computation techniques while addressing the specific requirements of sliding window diffusion.

Window-Diffusion (Zuo et al. 2026) addresses this by restricting attention to a sliding window around the decoding frontier ... Window-Diffusion couples two distinct operations at each phase boundary ... We propose Overlap-Refresh, which introduces two independent scheduling parameters.
